qt: to the Commission Loucas Fourlas (PPE) Subject:

According to Eurostat data, in Member States such as Cyprus, Greece and Romania, the share of utilised agricultural area managed by farms using precision farming technologies was very low, i.e. below 10 %. By contrast, Member States such as Luxembourg, Finland and Estonia recorded rates upwards of 75 %. In view of the above: In what ways and with what concrete measures does the Commission intend to reduce the gap between Member States in terms of use of precision technologies in agriculture?
at: (English version) to the Commission Loucas Fourlas (PPE) (1 September 2026) Subject: Technology and precision farming practices According to Eurostat data, in Member States such as Cyprus, Greece and Romania, the share of utilised agricultural area managed by farms using precision farming technologies was very low, i.e. below 10%. By contrast, Member States such as Luxembourg, Finland and Estonia recorded rates upwards of 75%. In view of the above: In what ways and with what concrete measures does the Commission intend to reduce the gap between Member States in terms of use of precision technologies in agriculture? (5 November 2026) The Commission is putting in place an enabling framework (1), for digitalisation in the agri-food sector for precision farming technologies that combines horizontal investments in computing capacity, AI infrastructure and data with sector-specific instruments, supporting the development, testing and uptake of digital and AI solutions by farmers. Under the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) several support instruments are available to enhance the up-take of precision farming technologies, such as investments on-farm and off-farm, and knowledge transfer and cooperation activities. In this framework, Member States are also required to develop a Digital Strategy as part of the CAP Strategic Plans (2) for the agricultural sector to accompany the digital transition in agriculture and rural areas. These actions have been expanded in the proposals for the CAP for the period 2028-2034 in the framework of the National and Regional Partnership (NRP) Plans. In this respect, the digital transition will benefit of new synergies and complementarities that Member States can explore both within the future NRP, including the CAP, as well as under the upcoming European Competitiveness Fund and the next Horizon Europe 2028-2034, where on-farm innovative solutions can be supported and complemented by broader public investments in broadband infrastructures. These efforts are complemented by additional actions supporting the development and deployment of precision farming. The Common European Agricultural Data Space aims to enable trusted and interoperable agricultural data sharing, while Copernicus provides Earth-observation data for crop, soil and climate monitoring, and Galileo/EGNOS provide high-accuracy positioning for precision farming.
